evidence.excerpt: Quantifying measurement uncertainty in radiated emissions tests is essential for reproducible compliance assessment under the Radio Equipment Directive. This study applies the CISPR 16-4-2 framework to a set of twelve 868 MHz short-range devices tested on a 3 m open-area test site and a semi-anechoic chamber. Six uncertainty contributors are evaluated: antenna factor calibration, receiver bandwidth, cable impedance mismatch, site imperfections expressed as normalised site attenuation deviation, ambient noise floor, and device positioning repeatability. The combined expanded uncertainty (k=2) ranged from 3.8 dB to 6.1 dB depending on frequency and device category. Comparison of results between the two test environments showed systematic differences of up to 2.3 dB for horizontally polarised emissions, consistent with ground-plane reflection variations. A simplified uncertainty budget worksheet suited to laboratory accreditation audits is presented. The findings suggest that the standard 6 dB margin applied in many pre-compliance workflows is insufficient for devices operating near the regulatory limit.
